what: Approve latency on the deployed API after batch 2 (PR #103, main e388a4b). Six wall-clock samples on the two hero plays (three Tea, three chips), plus one sample each on two other seeded plays. Same method and schema as approve_timing_2026-10-12b.json.
measured_at: about 11:25 IST, minutes after the deploy and the green smoke job of main run 38349023772
service_revision: taal-agents-00141-lhz, serving 100% of traffic (taal-web-00079-pp5 for the web service)

method.tool: curl, one POST per sample; seconds is the wall time of that request (time_total)
method.instance: warm: the instance had just served the post-deploy smoke job, so no sample is a first call after idle. No cold first call was measured in this set; the first call after idle still takes longer (about 8 to 12 s per the 12 Oct measurements) and is not part of the published range.
method.visitor: a fresh X-Taal-Visitor value for every call, so each approve starts from a new visitor store

summary.published_range: about 2 to 3 s warm (measured 13 Oct after batch 2; first call after idle takes longer)

caveat: Eight samples from a few minutes of one morning, not a percentile estimate. The range is what was measured, not a service-level target. Every sample carried stored, BigQuery-generated copy (copy.source existing, provenance bigquery_pregenerated), so none of them waited on a model call inside Approve.
history: approve_timing_2026-10-13.json holds the earlier 13 Oct samples taken right after batch 1 (about 1.3 to 3.3 s, some templated copy); approve_timing_2026-10-12.json (pre-#90) and approve_timing_2026-10-12b.json (after #90, 3.3 to 6.8 s) stay unchanged
